ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: At a temperature of 310K, decompose $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ through the reaction equation $2\text{N}_2\text{O}_5(g) \rightarrow 4\text{NO}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g)$; the kinetic data for this reaction are collected in the figure below. Based on the given data, find the value of the rate constant $k$ for this reaction, in units of $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a kinetic data table, with the left column being Time (s) and the right column being [N2O5] (M). The data in the table are: at 0 s, [N2O5]=0.250 M; at 500 s, it is 0.190 M; at 1000 s, it is 0.145 M; at 2000 s, it is 0.085 M. Then reason: The unit of the rate constant required by the problem is s^-1, so treat it as a first-order decomposition reaction. The integrated equation for a first-order reaction is k = ln([N2O5]0/[N2O5]t)/t. Taking the data at 0 s and 2000 s in the chart, k = ln(0.250/0.085)/2000 = ln(2.941176...)/2000 ≈ 1.0788/2000 = 5.39×10^-4 s^-1. According to significant figures, take k ≈ 5.4×10^-4 s^-1.
